description:
The current tests exercise many local invariants but do not establish the complete transaction contract across batching, materialization, persistence and recovery.

At `8f962e09`, the default suite passed (17 doctests, 158 properties, 2,891 tests; two excluded), and the explicit MinIO durability suite passed (two tests), while targeted production-module reproductions demonstrated mutation-order, empty-range conflict, endpoint, and compaction-version defects.

[test/bedrock/distributed/minio_durability_test.exs](https://github.com/bedrock-kv/bedrock/blob/8f962e09b24765265eeb6bd818f5b26da8d91b99/test/bedrock/distributed/minio_durability_test.exs#L109) exercises a Demux with three shards against MinIO and an injected transient object-write failure. It is useful persistence coverage, but it does not run a complete multi-node Repo transaction history through coordinator/director recovery. Existing GitHub #8 concerns coverage percentage; this issue concerns an independent semantic oracle and failure schedules.

## Bounded initial scope

- Run real Repo transactions through sequencer, proxies, resolvers, logs and materializers.
- Use a small independent sequential KV/mutation interpreter and a history checker that respects real-time order and commit-result ambiguity.
- Workloads: conditional inserts after empty range reads, conflicting point reads, same-key atomics in shared batches, mixed sets/clears/range clears, and multi-key invariants.
- Scenarios: ordinary batching, compaction plus cold reload, crashes around WAL acknowledgment and snapshot publication, and an epoch transition with an in-flight tail.
- Add a multi-node scenario separating node/process loss from network unreachability and checking acknowledged writes survive recovery.
- Retain seeds, operation histories and fault schedules for replayable failures.

## Acceptance criteria

- Known counterexamples fail against the independent oracle on the affected revision and pass after their fixes.
- No acknowledged commit is lost, no uncommitted tail becomes a durable baseline, and snapshots correspond to their advertised versions.
- The harness does not replace core transaction components with mocks; focused unit tests remain complementary.
- Document exactly which distributed failures the suite exercises. This issue does not require a complete BEAM deterministic simulator as its first deliverable.
